Twelve Knots to the Han

STS-HS10-L4-13001400-HSGEO-TTM-API-01 • HS Geometry Grade 10 • Pythagorean Theorem Proved Through Triangle Similarity
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Two thousand years ago, Chinese surveyors carried a rope with twelve evenly spaced knots. Pulled tight so the corners landed at 3 knots, 4 knots, and 5 knots, that rope built a perfect square corner every time, and the rule behind it was written down as gougu in the Zhoubi Suanjing. Mission 01 sends the team back to watch it being used, then home to prove why it works. The board shows the proof: drop one line from the right angle and the big triangle splits into two smaller triangles that are the same shape as the whole one.
The rope has twelve knots split into 3, 4, and 5. Why does that split always make a right corner?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
